meta.title: OPS-SAT Firmware Modification
meta.description: This diagram captures the telecommand-driven firmware modification attack on the OPS-SAT cube sat, as described by J. Willbold et. al in  Space Odyssey: An Experimental Software Security Analysis of Satellites.

data.label: Lack of TC Authentication (from paper)
user_properties:
The COM radio is directly connected to the OBC, where the OBSW uses the CSP protocol, which offers eXtended Tiny Encryption Algorithm (XTEA) 
encryption and Hash-Based Message Authentication Codes (HMAC) authentication. However, these capabilities are disabled via a compile-time flag. 
Hence, the COM does not offer any protection, and external attackers can command the satellite by executing arbitrary TCs, which includes anyone with a custom GS.

data.label: Rogue GS
user_properties:
This corresponds to the "external attacker" model
described in the J.Willbold paper.

data.label: Ground Segment Model
user_properties: This model is inferred from the attacker model described in the paper. It is meant to capture a simplistic ground station/network.

data.label: Transmitter/Receiver Models
user_properties:
D3FEND's models of transmitters and receivers by definition incorporate front-end/back-end processing
components such as modulators/filters/etc., so they don't need to be modeled separately.

data.label: Software, Firmware, or Programmable Logic Manipulation
Space Segment Model
user_properties: Note that this is not a complete model of OPS-SAT, but rather includes the key components relevant to this attack.

meta.title: SPARTA EX-0014.04: Bus Traffic Replay
meta.description: A model of SPARTA EX-0001.02 along with related events and artifacts.

data.label: Bus Message Auth
user_properties:
Bus Message Authentication involves hashing the
bus message contents, the ID of the sender, and a
"freshness" value such as a monotonically increasing
counter. The freshness value is what prevents replay
attacks, as the bus controller/monitor should reject any
frames with an invalid freshness.

data.label: Spacecraft Model
user_properties:
This is a very basic model of a spacecraft (satellite)
that is used to help illustrate this technique.

This condition captures the fact that the signal strength

meta.title: SPARTA IA-0002: Compromise Software Defined Radio
meta.description: A diagram depicting how IA-0002 is mapped and represented in D3FEND for Space.

data.label: Configuration vs. Waveform
user_properties:
Many SDR SoCs/platforms have well-defined register interfaces
for the RF front-end and separate logic/processing for the waveform, 
making independent modification straightforward. 


Examples: Xilinx RFSoC, AD9361

data.label: SDR Types
user_properties:
We define two types of SDRs: devices and computers.


SDR computers are considered to be self-contained radio
systems that have onboard compute capability (e.g., DSP, FPGA).
Example: Flexradio Flex-8400M


SDR devices are those without onboard computer and 
therfeore require a host computer for running the actual waveform. 
Example: RTL-SDR


On a spacecraft/satellite, you'd expect to see an SDR computer.

data.label: SDR Waveforms
user_properties:
We define SDR waveforms as software implementations of the set of transformations
applied to information to be transmitted and the corresponding set of transformations
to convert received signals back to their information content.


Example: a Software Communications Architecture (SCA) waveform application.

data.label: Software-defined Radio RF State Change Event

meta.title: SPARTA IOB CSNE-19: Unexpected High-Priority Messages on the CAN Bus
meta.description: Depicts how CSNE-19 is and bus traffic is represented in D3FEND for Space.

data.label: SPARTA IOB CSNE-19
user_properties:
Detection of unexpected high-priority CAN messages (lower message IDs) originating from unauthorized subsystems. 
This may indicate that a threat actor is injecting high-priority messages to dominate the CAN bus and manipulate subsystem communications.

meta.title: SPARTA IOB MIRE-5: Legitimate Command with Malicious Parameters Targeting Subsystems
meta.description: Depicts how IOB MIRE-5 is mapped to D3FEND for Space.

data.label: SPARTA IOB MIRE-5
user_properties: Detection of memory corruption in spacecraft flight software components, potentially caused by buffer overflow or other memory management vulnerabilities being exploited by threat actors..

data.label: SEE Threat Modeling
user_properties:
This simplified model shows the component-level
decomposition of a spacecraft, oriented around flight
software execution. It depicts the relationships between 
software and hardware components, highlighting the
potential down-stream effects on flight software when RAM
or CPU cache is corrupted by an SEE.

meta.title: SPARTA IOB UACE-10: Logs of Processed Commands Flooding
meta.description: A model of SPARTA IOB UACE-10, with related artifacts, events, and countermeasures.

data.label: SPARTA IOB UACE-10
user_properties:
Detection of an unusually high number of processed commands recorded in spacecraft logs, 
which may indicate a flooding attack using valid commands. Such a surge can overwhelm 
spacecraft processing capabilities, leading to resource exhaustion like CPU spikes, 
memory depletion, and increased battery usage. Monitoring log entries can reveal if 
the spacecraft is being flooded with valid but excessive commands, which could create 
denial of service conditions by saturating system processing resources.

data.label: Log Full
user_properties:
A log full event could be an indicator that the
event log has been flooded with valid commands.

data.label: TC
user_properties: This is the valid command produced by the attacker.

meta.title: SPARTA IOB UCEB-4: Unexpected Changes to Encryption Configuration Settings
meta.description: A model of IOB UCEB-4, with related artifacts, events, and countermeasures.

data.label: SPARTA IOB UCEB-4
user_properties:
Detection of unexpected changes to encryption settings, potentially indicating that
the encryption mechanism on the spacecraft has been disabled or bypassed without authorization.

data.label: Crypto Module
user_properties:
This example assumes that the spacecraft is using a hardware
cryptographic module for its crypto, but this could also be done in
software.

data.label: Cryptographic Module Operating Mode Change Event

meta.title: D3FEND for Space Overview
meta.description: An overview of the artifacts, relationships, and countermeasures added to the D3FEND ontology for D3FEND for Space. This is not meant to be complete or show all possible relationships and instead highlights some of the core concepts in the initial release of D3FEND for Space.

data.label: Ground Station Modeling
user_properties:
Our model of ground station components is a work in progress and will likely be updated with specific subclasses (e.g., Antenna Controller) in a 
future release.


Typical enterprise IT assets such as servers, workstations, etc. that may be found at a ground station are already modeled in D3FEND.

data.label: GNSS sub-model
user_properties:
This is our first pass at a GNSS model, and we expect to flesh it out with additional classes for things like Ephemeris
and PNT Solutions as well as specific countermeasures in a future release.

data.label: Sensors and Actuators
user_properties:
We expect to refine these classes with
space-specific sub-classes such as Star Trackers
and Magnetorquers as well as non domain-specific
sensors such as Thermometers (thermal transducer
sensors) in a future release.

data.label: EMAG Rad Hardening
user_properties:
This countermeasure can be applied to any device
that is a sub-class of d3f:HardwareDevice.

data.label: Safe Mode
user_properties:
This is currently the only spacecraft-specific
operating mode that we have modeled, but
more may be added in a future release.

data.label: Wireless Link
user_properties:
Instances of d3f:WirelessLink can be used to represent Satellite
Uplinks and Downlinks.

data.label: Watchdog Timers
user_properties:
Our model of watchdog timers also includes hardware
watchdog timers, which may be built into an embedded CPU
contained within a physically separate chip.

data.label: Vehicle Software
user_properties:
This class is meant to encompass any type of software
running on a vehicle. Currently, we have specific 
sub-classes for Vehicle Control Software but more may be
added in a future release.

data.label: Signals
user_properties:
Signals in our model can carry any form of d3f:DigitalInformation,
including things like Telecommands, Software, and Cryptographic Keys.

meta.title: Satellite User Terminal Example
meta.description: A generalized example of a satellite user terminal modeled with D3FEND for Space artifacts.

data.label: User Terminal
user_properties: The complete ground-based system that allows a user or local network to communicate through a satellite. It includes RF equipment, modem/baseband processing, networking, power, control, and user interfaces.

data.label: Outdoor Unit (ODU)
user_properties: The externally mounted portion of the terminal that interfaces directly with the satellite RF link. It typically includes the antenna, transmit and receive RF electronics, filtering, amplification, and pointing hardware.

data.label: Indoor Unit (IDU)
user_properties: The indoor or user-accessible portion of the terminal that performs modem, networking, management, and power functions. In some modern systems, IDU functions may be integrated into the ODU or a single terminal enclosure.

data.label: Local User Device
user_properties: A representative client device such as a laptop or phone connected behind the router. It is included to complete the user-facing end of the end-to-end path and to show where decoded and routed traffic ultimately lands.

data.label: Local User Device
user_properties: A representative client device such as a laptop or phone connected behind the Starlink router. It is included to complete the user-facing end of the end-to-end path and to show where decoded and routed traffic ultimately lands. T.

data.label: Satellite Modem
user_properties: The baseband device that converts user data into a satellite waveform for transmission and converts received satellite waveforms back into user data. It handles modulation, demodulation, coding, framing, synchronization, and link control.

data.label: RF Transceiver
user_properties: The RF transceiver (including front-end) used by the terminal for bidirectional communication.

data.label: GNSS Receiver
user_properties: User terminals may incorporate a GNSS receiver for position and timing information.

data.label: Power Supply
user_properties: The component that converts external power into the voltages required by the terminal. It may power only the IDU or also provide power to the ODU over coax, Ethernet, or a dedicated cable.

data.label: IDU Modeling
user_properties:
IDUs typically contain router/wireless router functionality,
which is why we use d3f:Router here for their base class.
Otherwise, it would likely be d3f:EmbeddedComputer.

data.label: Firmware
user_properties:
The firmware image running on the IDU,
usually capable of being updated by the
SatCom provider.
